subject: Amplitude filtering before ACI calculation of multiple files

messages.author: c0c0814d6b448539
messages.subject: Amplitude filtering before ACI calculation of multiple files
parts:
I need to calculate Acoustic Complexity Index (ACI) of hundreds of .wav files as part of a Soundscape Ecology study.


The soundecology package in R has a very useful function multiple_sounds () function. However, I couldn't find any amplitude filter in the package.


seewave package has afilter () which allows to set filtering of amplitude by setting at certain thresholds.


I would like to use afilter () to many .wav files in a folder and then to apply multiple_sounds () to all the filtered files. Since I am new to R, I am at a loss to combine or loop these two functions to get desired results.


Can you please help me in this?


Examples:


afilter (.wav files,f=22050,threshold= 5,plot= F)

multiple_sounds (directory = "C:/Users/pc1/Desktop/sound",
            resultfile = "C:/Users/pc1/Desktop/sound/results1.csv",
            soundindex = "acoustic_complexity",min_freq = 1500, max_freq = 
            12000, j = 5, fft_w = 512)


Thank you,


Ana

Hi Ana,

I am also an R novice, so bear with me, but perhaps you could just use a for loop?
There are surely more efficient ways to process through a directory...

I think the key is to get each .wav file recognized, then seewave (or soundscape) can work.
For example,

library(tuneR)
library(seewave)
#create an empty space for results to be stored
result=NULL
output=NULL
# create directory
l<-list.files("/yourdirectory",full.names = T)
# write a for loop to sequence through directory for the total number of files in directory
for (i in length(l)){
  #read each file, as a single object
  y1<-i
  y2<-readWave(y1)
  y3<-afilter(y2,f=22050,threshold= 5,plot= F)
  # then write file, or do whatever is next
  # result=ACI(y3)
  # output<-rbind(result,output)
  }

I hope this is helpful.

Adam

messages.author: 1f04514119422e67
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: Amplitude filtering before ACI calculation of multiple files
parts:
I think you can simplify the code a bit if you use the package "purrr" (yes, with three Rs), avoiding the for(). The map function is a bit like a simplified apply(), as in it applies the desired function to a given list. 

The code can be further streamlined by using pipes, but I think way is easier for novices to understand what is happening in each line (and to debug any errors). It may require a lot of memory if the files are big, as it reads all files before calculating the index, in which case the for() solution may be a better option, as files are read one by one

library(purrr) # map() function
library(seewave) # ACI() function

files<-list.files()
waves <- map(files, readWave)  # reads all files in directory into a list
filtered <- map(waves, afilter, f=22050,threshold= 5,plot= F, output="Wave") # filters files read in line above, returning a list
ACIS <- map_dbl(filtered, ACI) # calculates ACI for each filtered sound, returning a vector of values

Cheers,
 Vitor
